subject: Immediate: NutriOnix production tail-latency surge — C-suite liaison & stabilization plan
messages:
From: Oliver Crane <oliver.crane@nutrionix.io>
To: support@nutrionix.io, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 22:14:00 -0800
Subject: NutriOnix prod: sudden tail-latency spikes impacting checkout

Rishi,

We're seeing a sharp increase in tail latency and 5xx errors on our product search and checkout endpoints since ~18:30 PST. P95 for text-gen calls jumping from ~280ms to 1.8s; error rate up from 0.2% to 2.4%. This is causing checkout timeouts for ~3% of paying traffic. Our ops team is standing by and can share traces. Can you confirm this is on Redwood's side and what mitigation you can apply immediately?

Attachment: slo-metrics-20261210.csv (summary export)

Thanks,
Oliver
VP Eng, NutriOnix
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 9 Dec 2026 22:27:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: NutriOnix prod: sudden tail-latency spikes impacting checkout

Forwarding incoming escalation from NutriOnix. Key asks: 1) immediate mitigation to reduce tail latency and error rate; 2) clear customer comms and C-suite liaison; 3) rollback/capacity options and ETA.

Current telemetry (from their CSV): p50 ~240ms, p95 ~1.8s, p99 ~3.6s, error rate 2.4%. Affected routes: /v1/generate (search), /v1/chat/complete (checkout bot).

Proposed immediate steps (please ack):
- Laura: pull runbook snapshot, confirm whether recent model variant rollout or config change matches incident window.
- Marissa: spin up dedicated burst fleet (if available) and enable fallback to smaller quantized variant for non-critical paths.
- Ben: craft short customer-facing note and coordinates with NutriOnix execs; include credits/SLAs options.
- Hannah: start an exec bridge and prepare one-pager for C-suite.

I'll be on the bridge. Tag me in Ops channel once resources are live.

--
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 00:12:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: NutriOnix prod: sudden tail-latency spikes impacting checkout

Rishi — initial findings: no config deploys in production at 18:30 PST per audit trail. However, we rolled a scheduling tweak to batcher thresholds in staging earlier today (11:00 PST) that may have been promoted via a templated job; investigating correlation.

Attached runbook_snapshot.pdf with current autoscaling knobs and fallback variants. Next actions:
- I will run targeted KV cache warmers for the top 20 prefixes and clear any stalled worker queues. ETA 20m.
- If error rates don't decline, suggest enabling constant small-variant routing for checkout flows to reduce latency variance.

I'll post trace snippets to OPS-9123 in 10m.

Laura
Sr Manager, Serving Runtime
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 00:41:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: NutriOnix prod: sudden tail-latency spikes impacting checkout

On it — I spun up two reserved burst GPU pools in us-west-2 and enabled route-level fallback to the q4_8bit variant for non-authenticated search traffic. Checkout routes are currently pinned to the production model but we can start a gradual canary to q4_8bit for 10% traffic immediately.

Actions taken:
- +2 burst pools (estimated capacity +40% for affected routes)
- Canary fallback 10% on /v1/generate, monitoring error rate and p95 in 5m windows
- Warmed KV cache for top prefixes (as Laura requested)

Preliminary telemetry after 12 minutes: p95 down to 720ms on canary traffic; overall p95 at ~1.1s; error rate trending down to 1.1% (previously 2.4%).

Marissa
Director, Production Ops
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Crane <oliver.crane@nutrionix.io>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 01:05:00 -08:00
Subject: NutriOnix incident: immediate mitigation and next steps

Oliver — thanks for flagging and for the CSV. Quick status: we identified a scheduling misalignment that increased batching variance; we applied KV warming and activated burst capacity. We also started a 10% canary to the q4_8bit variant which shows improved tail behavior.

What we are doing now:
- Continue canary expansion to 30% in 20 minutes contingent on error rate staying <1.5%
- Keep burst pools active and monitor cost delta; we'll provide transparency on temporary overage and propose a credits package if the incident affects SLA metrics for December.
- Daily post-mortem and action items delivered to you by EOD tomorrow.

Customer ask: please advise if immediate rollback to the previous model variant on checkout is preferred to canary expansion. If you want us to force 100% to q4_8bit, we can do so but will need 8-12 minutes to flush and warm caches.

Ben Carter
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Oliver Crane <oliver.crane@nutrionix.io>, laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 15:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Executive summary for NutriOnix C-suite — incident stabilization and next steps

Oliver / NutriOnix execs — thank you for patience. Short executive summary for your leadership:
- Incident window: 2026-12-09 18:30 PST — 2026-12-10 01:15 PST (major stabilization achieved; monitoring continues)
- Impact: transient p95 increase affecting search and checkout, peak user-facing error rate ~2.4%, estimated 3% of paying sessions experienced timeout failures during peak
- Immediate mitigations: KV cache warmers, +2 burst GPU pools (us-west-2), 10% canary to q4_8bit then stepped to 30% after positive telemetry — reduced p95 from 1.8s to ~650ms on canary; overall error rate down to ~0.6%
- Customer options provided: full rollback to prior production model (estimated 10min disruption), or continued canary expansion with per-minute telemetry and credits if SLA breach confirmed
- Commitments: full post-mortem with timeline, root cause, and corrective actions by EOD tomorrow; proactive runbook changes to prevent scheduler drift; proposed goodwill credit to be discussed with finance

Next immediate ask from NutriOnix: preferred mitigation path (rollback vs canary expansion). Once we have preference we will proceed and notify execs.

Rishi Malhotra
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
Attachment: runbook_snapshot.pdf
